summary: Essex County, VT lookout on Stone Mountain in Guildhall, begun 1922 and staffed into 1971; FFLA lists it and its West Topsham relocation as gone.

facts.design: Fire tower with a separate lookout cabin
facts.status_note: FFLA lists the Stone Mountain tower and the West Topsham relocation as gone; no source describes either site now.

events.note: August 1922: construction started on a new tower on Stone Mountain; completion not described
New lookout cabin begun; old cabin moved for wood storage (term ending June 30, 1938)
October 1948 Essex County Herald: a man employed at the fire tower
Tower ventilator replaced with a weatherproof cap (biennial report covering 1949-50)
Commercial phone line passed within a mile of the station; state connected its tower line and salvaged three miles of pole line (1957-58 report)
May 1971 News and Citizen: a woman stationed on Stone Mountain to be in charge of the fire tower
FFLA lists a relocated Stone Mountain site at West Topsham, Orange County, as a radio tower, gone; no date or mover in sources

evidence.supports: Stone Mountain is in Guildhall, Essex County, Vermont
August 1922 item is from the Bennington Evening Banner
August 1922: construction started on a new tower on Stone Mountain in Guildhall, with cabins
evidence.quote: Construction has been started on two fire towers and cabins in Essex county, one on Stone mountain in Guildhall to be built new.

evidence.supports: the new tower would let watchers see heavily timbered country no other tower could see
evidence.quote: The new tower will permit the observance of heavily timbered country not visible from any other tower.

evidence.supports: the state forestry department ran the lookout program in 1922
evidence.quote: C.C. Delavan of the State forestry department is in the northern part of the State on an inspection trip.

evidence.supports: 1938: new lookout cabin begun with log lean-to, fireplaces and tables
evidence.quote: Began construction of new lookout cabin, log leanto shelter, fireplaces, and tables.

evidence.supports: 1938: old cabin moved to serve as wood storage
evidence.quote: Moved old cabin for use as wood storage.

evidence.supports: 1949-50: tower ventilator replaced with weatherproof cap
evidence.quote: Replaced tower ventilator with weatherproof cap.

evidence.supports: 1957-58: commercial phone line within a mile of station; state connected and salvaged three miles of pole line
evidence.quote: The lines passed within a mile of Stone Mountain station at which point we were able to make a connection to the fire tower line and discontinue and salvage three miles of pole line.

evidence.supports: October 1948: a man was employed at the fire tower and his family spent the summer there
evidence.quote: Mr. and Mrs. Ira Daniels and family have returned home after spending the summer at Stone Mt. where Mr. Daniels is employed at the Fire Tower.

evidence.supports: May 1971: a woman stationed on Stone Mountain in Guildhall to be in charge of the fire tower
evidence.quote: She is stationed on Stone Mt. in the town of Guildhall, Vermont. She will be in charge of the fire tower.

evidence.supports: FFLA lists the Stone Mountain tower as gone
FFLA lists a relocated Stone Mountain site at West Topsham, Orange County, as a radio tower, gone
evidence.quote: (Relocated Stone Mountain) Orange 44.11666 -72.31056 Radio Tower Gone

evidence.supports: the clippings page carries a National Geodetic Survey entry for a Stone Mtn Lookout Tower marker
the page carries the word Removed near that entry; no date or explanation given

sources.title: Vermont Fire Towers - Forest Fire Lookout Association

notes_for_editor: The West Topsham relocation rests only on one FFLA list line; no source gives a date, mover or site description, and no source describes what stands there. The record's name 'now at West Topsham' implies a structure on site, which conflicts with FFLA's gone status; the record's kind 'tower' differs from FFLA's 'Radio Tower' label for West Topsham. Both left for a human decision, not proposed as corrections. The word 'Removed' on the Forest Lookouts page may be a page-wide status label rather than a fact about the tower or its survey marker; the Forest Lookouts page for Baldy Mountain in Washington carries the same word, so treat it as unexplained. The original Stone Mountain site also has a separate record (us-vt-stone-mountain) with the same sources.
